card: sc_hysek_2014 (data/study-cards/mdma.json), first-pass by AI reader 64 from PMC HTML
source_read: PDF PDFs/MDMA/Hysek_2014_MDMAEmpathyProsocial.pdf.pdf (version of record, SCAN 9:1645-1652), all 8 pages; text extracted and pp. 1646-1649 rendered at 150 dpi, Figures 2, 3 and 4E re-read at 300 dpi. Supplementary data not among the files.
reference_record: hysek_2014 agrees with the PDF (title, authors, Social Cognitive and Affective Neuroscience 9(11):1645-1652, 2014; advance access 4 October 2013).

items.card_says: The inequality-aversion test (F(1,20) = 3.39) is printed without saying which volunteers were analysed.
items.pdf_says: The test was run 'in subjects with a prosocial orientation'; only their number is not given (20 error degrees of freedom).
items.page: p. 1647, Results > Social Value Orientation, 1st paragraph (continuing in the right column)

items.card_says: Peak plasma MDMA higher in women (269.9 ng/mL) than in men (209 ng/mL).
items.pdf_says: Those are the text's mean Cmax values (p. 1648), but Figure 4E's mean concentration curves peak at only about 183 ng/mL (men) and 194 ng/mL (women) at 2.5 hours (editors' reading at 300 dpi), a much smaller sex difference; the gap is unexplained, and the sex comparison is printed with F(1,15) although each sex has 16.
items.page: pp. 1648-1649, Results > Endocrine effects and pharmacokinetics, 2nd paragraph; Figure 4E

items.card_says: The size of any effect cannot be known; means are only in Figures 1 to 3 and Supplementary Table S1 (not read); no means or SDs for any outcome are printed in the text.
items.pdf_says: The PDF's figures are legible vector graphics. Editors' approximate readings: explicit emotional empathy (1-9 scale) placebo against MDMA, all 4.4 against 5.0, women 5.0 against 5.2, men 3.9 against 4.9; implicit, all 4.3 against 4.8, men 3.8 against 4.8, women 4.8 against 4.8; cognitive empathy about 62% in both conditions; SVO angle all 31 against 37 degrees, women 37 against 37, men 26 against 37; inequality-aversion index all 0.48 against 0.38; oxytocin change about 12 against 66 pg/mL; VAS 'happy' peak about 25 to 30 on an axis from -50 to 50 whose scale the paper does not define. The text does print pharmacokinetic means with SEM (Cmax, AUC, Tmax) and dose per kg with SD.
items.page: pp. 1647-1649, Figures 1-4; p. 1648, Results > Endocrine effects and pharmacokinetics

items.card_says: Bedi et al. (2010), as cited by these authors: raised self-rated sociability.
items.pdf_says: Hysek et al. do cite Bedi et al. (2010) for increased self-rated sociability (p. 1648, Discussion, 1st paragraph), but Bedi et al.'s own results show only methamphetamine significantly raised self-rated sociability; MDMA 1.5 mg/kg raised loving and friendliness (card sc_bedi_2010; Bedi author manuscript PDF pp. 5-6). The entry can now carry reference bedi_2010.

items.card_says: as measured in a hospital laboratory
items.pdf_says: Where the sessions took place is not stated (the authors are at University Hospital Basel).
Random order is stated only in the abstract; the Methods describe a double-blind, placebo-controlled cross-over design without mentioning randomization.
MDMA affected recognition accuracy for fearful and sad faces differently in men and women: F(1,31) = 6.61, P = 0.015, and F(1,31) = 9.42, P = 0.005.
items.page: p. 1647, Results > Facial emotion recognition, 1st paragraph

items.pdf_says: In women, fear recognition accuracy correlated inversely with MDMA Cmax (Rp = -0.62, P = 0.014) and AUC0-6h (Rp = -0.66, P = 0.006), n = 16; the minus signs are visible on the rendered page but lost in the text layer. Editors' calculation: r = -0.62 with n = 16 gives p of about 0.010; P = 0.014 fits n = 15.
items.page: pp. 1647-1648, Results > Facial emotion recognition, 1st paragraph (continuing at the top of p. 1648, left column)

items.pdf_says: The Discussion describes 'a trend reduction in inequality-aversion', whereas by the paper's own definition (index 0 = perfect inequality aversion) the lower index means a shift towards inequality aversion, as the Results say.

The limitations say a dose-response study was not done to avoid exposing the mostly drug-naive subjects to more than two doses of MDMA, although the Methods describe one MDMA session per person; with two trial registrations, the sessions may belong to larger studies the paper does not describe.
AUC0-6h 926.8 (SEM 29.3) in men and 1146.5 (SEM 37.9) ng/ml h in women, F(1,15) = 20.77; Tmax 2.44 h (SEM 0.14), 2.10 (0.20) in men and 2.75 (0.17) in women.
items.page: p. 1648, Results > Endocrine effects and pharmacokinetics, 2nd paragraph
